note: Concrete example based on the bread-demand forecasting dataset. Illustrates time-series guardrails: chronological split only (no random CV), MASE with lag-7 naive baseline, residual ACF diagnostic, concurrent-feature audit, and the overfitting assessment scale. Also illustrates the proposed `mlflow` output block (step 14a) — populated here as if logging succeeded; all four fields would be null if step 14a was skipped or failed.

context.reason: recommended_strategy and metric choices carry forward to Training

recommended_strategy.narrative: Mixed feature types (OHE categoricals, sparse weather, lag numerics) favour tree-based models over linear. No scaling needed. Embedded selection via feature importance.

recommended_metric.reasoning: MAE is interpretable in units of bread loaves. MASE normalises against the lag-7 naive baseline so performance is benchmarked against the simplest seasonal forecast, not just an absolute number.

input.mode_reasoning: First Training call this run — no prior model exists to compare against.

output.reasoning: EDA recommended tree-based models given mixed feature types (OHE categoricals, sparse weather columns with NaN, lag numerics). LightGBM chosen over XGBoost for native NaN handling in remaining weather columns and faster iteration.

n_estimators.reasoning: default starting point; early stopping will find the effective number

max_depth.reasoning: moderate depth prevents memorisation of weekly patterns without underfitting the regime interaction

learning_rate.reasoning: slow enough to generalise across the 9-year trend

num_leaves.reasoning: LightGBM default; revisit if Diagnosis finds underfitting

subsample.reasoning: row subsampling adds regularisation for a dataset with known distribution shift (train vs val means differ)

colsample_bytree.reasoning: feature subsampling; consistent with embedded posture — model will prune weak features via importance

min_child_samples.reasoning: prevents leaf splits on tiny groups; particularly relevant for sparse Monday rows

early_stopping_rounds.reasoning: stops before overfitting using val set as monitor; effective n_estimators recorded after fit

MASE.interpretation: train predictions 64.8% better than the lag-7 naive baseline on training data
val predictions 39.4% better than the lag-7 naive baseline — model beats seasonal naive but gap is meaningful

metrics.metric_assessment: MAE of 31.7 bread units on validation represents ~11.9% of the validation set mean demand (~266 units). MASE of 0.606 confirms the model beats the seasonal naive forecast, but the train-to-val MAE gap (18.4 vs 31.7, ratio 1.72) indicates moderate overfitting. Diagnosis should investigate whether feature count, the 8 concurrent features, or the train/val distribution shift (train mean 325.8 vs val mean 283.5) is the primary driver.

overfitting_check.note: Ratio 1.72 falls in the 1.25-2.0 moderate range. Likely contributors: 8 concurrent same-day features give the model near-perfect retrospective signal on training days; the val set covers the 2019-2020 regime transition period which was underrepresented in training. Diagnosis should test: (1) remove concurrent features to see effect on val MAE, (2) increase min_child_samples.

feature_importance.note: concurrent feature — high importance expected but not available at inference in live_forecast scenario
< 0.5% of total importance — candidate for Diagnosis to drop

residuals_summary.bias_note: Small positive mean residual (3.2) — model very slightly under-predicts on average on validation set.

2019-H2.note: slightly over-predicts (negative = predicted > actual) in the post-train transition period

2020-H1.note: under-predicts in early 2020 — likely regime transition effect (store opened Mondays mid-2020)

2020-H2.note: under-predicts in regime-change period; model may not have fully captured Monday demand ramp-up

lag_1.note: below 0.2 threshold — acceptable residual autocorrelation at lag-1

lag_7.note: low seasonal residual autocorrelation — lag-7 feature is absorbing the weekly cycle adequately

residual_acf.assessment: Residual autocorrelation is within acceptable bounds. The temporal bias in early 2020 is the main signal: the model under-predicts during the regime transition. Diagnosis hypothesis: the regime transition captured by store_open_7_7 may need a more granular representation for the specific Monday ramp-up period.

clarification_needed.description: The deployment scenario is unspecified. The current model was trained and evaluated including 8 concurrent same-day operational features (num_orders, total_revenue, distinct_waitresses, avg_order_value_log1p, num_orders_with_reduction_log1p, pct_ticket_printed, num_distinct_payment_modes, top_payment_mode_count). These features ranked 3rd, 6th, and 10th in feature importance. If this model is intended for live day-ahead forecasting, those features are unavailable at prediction time and the model should be retrained on pre_period features only. Please confirm: retrospective analysis or live day-ahead forecast?

agent_initiated_findings.title: Train-val distribution shift contributes to moderate overfitting gap
agent_initiated_findings.method: Comparison of split-level bread_quantity means from Preprocess report
agent_initiated_findings.findings: Train mean=325.8, val mean=283.5 — a 13% drop. The model was trained on higher-demand years and evaluated on lower-demand years. Some of the train-val MAE gap (18.4 vs 31.7) reflects genuine distributional shift, not purely model overfitting.
agent_initiated_findings.reasoning: A model trained on a higher mean and evaluated on a lower mean will tend to over-predict, widening the absolute MAE gap even if the model's relative fit is unchanged. The overfitting ratio of 1.72 is therefore an upper bound on true overfitting — the distributional shift is baked in. Diagnosis should account for this when interpreting the metric.
